narrative: Two tickets eight months apart, both routine: currency formatting dropped in an export, and an alert-threshold setting that took a few tries to configure. Both resolved within a week with no recurrence or complaint beyond the original ask. A quiet, low-touch, healthy account with nothing to act on.

Five tickets over nine months, all minor operational questions (dashboard lag, seat permissions, alert delay) resolved in days. The most recent ticket flags a recurring rather than one-off problem: "We have to re-enter the ERP connector credentials about once a month even though nothing's changed on our side. Minor annoyance but recurring." Otherwise routine, engaged, healthy traffic.

Six calm, evenly-spaced tickets over eight months, but two threads never actually close. A bulk-permission-template request from January is still just being checked on in August ("raised back in January, are on the roadmap at all"), and a missing API field found in June turns out in July to be "missing from a second endpoint too. Might be a wider gap in the schema." No anger anywhere — the customer is patiently tracking open items support hasn't closed, which is the quiet accumulation pattern worth watching rather than loud friction.

Four tickets over ten months — a licence-count reconciliation, an export button that vanished and later reappeared with a new (fixed) cutoff bug, and a heads-up on API volume nearly doubling. Neutral, practical tone throughout, all resolved within a week. A healthy, low-drama account.

Five well-documented tickets over five months, and one thread never actually gets fixed: folder-level seat permissions set up in September are reported in February as reverting on their own — "it turns out the scoping only holds for a few weeks before newly added dashboards default back to visible-to-all for the affected seats. We've caught this twice now by manually auditing folder access each month, which isn't sustainable but works well enough that we've built it into our onboarding checklist." The customer explicitly says "No urgent need to escalate, just flagging in case it's a known limitation" — exactly the quiet, workaround-adopted, no-real-fix pattern that precedes non-renewal rather than loud anger.

Eight tickets across 16 months, consistently warm: feature requests, thank-yous, and an explicit "the new drill-down feature on dashboards is excellent. Genuinely means we've stopped pulling anything into Excel for the monthly review now, which is exactly what we hoped for when we signed up." The only open item is a self-described "not urgent at all" cosmetic tile-alignment issue. A model healthy account.

competitor_mentions.quote: We evaluated Storsund BI briefly last year and one of the reasons we stayed was speed, so this is worth getting ahead of.
Storsund BI apparently supports it natively, is it something Kataja could add?

narrative: Six practical, low-drama tickets over 18 months, but the account names a competitor twice: it evaluated Storsund BI on speed grounds before staying, and later asked whether Kataja could match a connector Storsund BI already supports. Both mentions are informational rather than active shopping, and every ticket resolves cleanly, but the competitor is clearly a known fallback in this customer's mind.

Seven tickets over ten months, uniformly positive: "Reports have looked great since the seat additions in the autumn — thanks for the smooth support all year," "Everything else is running smoothly on our end." All feature requests or how-tos, fast resolutions, no recurring faults. A healthy, growing account.

An 11-ticket arc from February to July 2024 that escalates from routine bug reports to open anger — "This is now the third separate module with issues in a month. Our team has basically stopped trying to use the platform," "Someone senior needs to own this" — and then quietly resigns rather than resolves: by June the team is "building workarounds in other tools," and by July tickets read "I'll be honest — I'm not sure it's worth going into detail at this point" and log a persistent Report Builder bug "for completeness" with a manual workaround instead of a real fix. The dangerous part isn't the anger, it's that the arc ends in resignation, not resolution.

Two low-key tickets four months apart, both Report Builder filter/date quirks, both resolved within days and framed calmly ("same spirit as the filter issue back in November, just a smaller nuisance"). Sparse, neutral traffic with no tension — a healthy quiet account.

A high-volume, chronically bumpy account across roughly two years — connector, API, dashboard and admin faults recur repeatedly, sometimes several in a single day ("Third connector failure this week" equivalents, e.g. "Second connector issue this week — starting to feel like a pattern") — but every incident is fixed within one to two days and the customer keeps engaging normally rather than pulling back or building workarounds. By August 2025 there's a hint of rising suspicion ("wondering if something's off with your auth system generally") but no resignation and no competitor talk. Loud but retained.

Four tickets over 13 months with consistently slow resolution times (8, 8, 11 days). A February request for two new finance seats with controller access came back wrong — "The two new seats from earlier this month went live but with viewer-only access rather than the controller permission set we asked for" — and this was never followed up or confirmed fixed before the account's next contact, seven months later, on an unrelated topic. Looks like a customer who stopped chasing rather than one whose issue was actually closed.

Sparse traffic, four tickets in 14 months, mostly routine questions. But a scheduled CSV export that lost its header row in August 2024 ("previously it always included one") was never followed up or confirmed fixed — the account's next contact, nine months later, is an unrelated API question. A quiet dropped issue, not a healthy silence.

Six tickets over a year, mostly resolving cleanly, but a January request for a read-only scoped API key resurfaces in May as a real security finding: "The read-only scoped key we set up back in January for the internal tool appears to have full write access based on what our security review just found." This is raised calmly and the account keeps transacting normally afterward, but the thread has no confirmed close — a substantive, unresolved security gap rather than routine friction.

13 tickets over eight months in tight, bursty clusters — Report Builder freezes losing an hour of work, dashboards stuck on stale numbers, an API outage the day before a board meeting — but every incident is fixed within a day or two, and the customer says so directly: "Rough week but the team got onto each one fast — noted and appreciated." Loud and volatile, but engaged and retained, not leaving.

13 tickets over nine months, another bursty-but-resolved account: cascading failures right after New Year and again through a rough week in July, each fixed within a day or two. Ends on an explicitly positive note — "That's the whole list cleared for this week — appreciate everyone jumping on it fast even if it was a lot" — with no workaround-building or resignation language anywhere in the record.

Four light-touch, purely administrative tickets over two months — file naming, an API usage question, retiring old alerts and dashboards. Entirely routine housekeeping with no friction whatsoever; a low-maintenance, unremarkable account.

12 tickets over nine months show the same faults recurring without ever being root-caused. Connectors fail four times in a single week ("Third connector failure this week. At this point I'd like someone to actually explain what's wrong rather than just restarting it each time"), API 403 errors return in April ("Getting the same 403 errors on the API we saw back in December"), and export corruption reappears in August ("Same symptom as earlier in the year, different report this time"). Every incident is patched fast, but the customer has explicitly noticed the pattern and is starting to push for a real explanation rather than another restart.

An 18-ticket account with a genuine turnaround. Chronic cross-module failures through late 2024 culminate in a February 2025 formal escalation ("I'd like a call with someone senior about what's actually going on"), and problems continue into April even after that. But from July onward the tone changes completely — "the changes since our call have made a real difference," "New seats were provisioned the same day I asked, first time that's happened," "dashboards have been fast and reliable for weeks now. Nice change from earlier in the year" — and the account ends the period expanding usage with a new connector and dashboard request. This is the escalation-then-genuine-resolution arc; risk has come down, not up.

Five long, meticulous tickets spread across 19 months — the quiet pattern that matters most. Real faults (alert threshold miscalibration flooding inboxes, Report Builder timing out on multi-entity consolidation, slow dashboards) each get a fix, but the underlying connector lag never does: the final ticket, five months after the others, reports it is "still running six to eight hours behind during month-end, same as it was in October," that the customer has "restructured our close process around a manual export into Excel," and is "raising it mainly so it's on record rather than expecting an urgent fix at this stage." A sophisticated finance customer has quietly built a permanent way around the platform's core reporting function and stopped expecting Kataja to fix it — high risk despite the calm tone and low ticket volume.
